Title: SAIGuard: Communication-State Simulation for Proactive Defense of LLM Multi-Agent Systems
Abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) solve complex tasks through inter-agent collaboration, but their communication-driven nature also allows security risks to spread across agents and trigger system-wide failures. Existing MAS defenses mainly follow a reactive paradigm after execution by detecting and isolating harmful agents, which may cause irreversible damage and degrade collaborative utility. To address this, we propose a proactive defense framework for MAS security, namely a Simulation-Aware Interception Guard (SAIGuard). SAIGuard performs communication-state simulation over the MAS interaction graph, estimates the impact of incoming messages on local agent states and the global MAS state, and detects risky messages via reconstruction deviations from benign communication patterns. Instead of isolating agents, SAIGuard sanitizes or regenerates suspicious messages before its propagation into the system. Experiments across diverse topologies and attack scenarios show that SAIGuard reduces attack success rates while maintaining MAS utility, outperforming reactive defenses.
Major_Contribution_Result: SAIGuard is a proactive defense for LLM multi-agent systems that simulates communication state on the interaction graph, detects risky messages via reconstruction deviations from benign patterns, and sanitizes or regenerates suspicious messages before execution instead of only isolating agents after harm. Experiments across diverse topologies, attacks, and backbone LLMs are reported to reduce attack success while maintaining MAS utility versus reactive defenses. The authors report improving collaborative utility by 11.96% and reducing average ASR by 67.47% in their evaluated settings.
Research_Limitations_Challenges: The authors state SAIGuard currently focuses on textual communication among agents and may not fully capture multimodal risks (images, audio, video), including visual prompt injection. Future work suggested includes multimodal encoders in communication-state simulation and modality-aware remediation.
Critics: This is a multi-agent mitigation paper centered on pre-execution communication interception, not a single-agent tool-IPI benchmark. The reported utility/ASR deltas are tied to the authors' topologies, attacks, and backbones and should not be treated as universal MAS security scores. It adds a proactive MAS evaluation angle for agent-security SLRs, without claiming a complete multimodal or supply-chain assurance lifecycle.
